content.stem: The PCN scheme is managed and administered by:
distractors: TWI Certification Ltd runs CSWIP, not PCN.
ASNT runs SNT-TC-1A, not PCN.
UKAS accredits BINDT; it does not run the scheme.
content.explanation: The PCN scheme is managed and administered by the British Institute of Non-Destructive Testing (BINDT).

content.stem: The PCN general requirements for NDT personnel are set out in the document:
distractors: SNT-TC-1A is the ASNT document, not PCN's.
That is the CSWIP scheme document, not PCN's.
CP-105 is an ASNT topical-outline document.
content.explanation: The general requirements for PCN certification are set out in PCN/GEN.

content.stem: PCN certification is accredited by UKAS against:
distractors: ISO 9001 covers quality management, not personnel certification.
17025 covers testing laboratories, not personnel.
API Q1 is a manufacturing quality spec.
content.explanation: BINDT operates PCN under UKAS accreditation to ISO/IEC 17024 for personnel certification.

content.stem: PCN qualification examinations are conducted at:
distractors: Exams are held at independent Authorised Qualifying Bodies.
Only approved AQBs run the examinations.
ASNT chapters are unrelated to PCN exams.
content.explanation: PCN examinations are conducted at Authorised Qualifying Bodies (AQBs) approved and monitored by BINDT.

content.stem: Under PCN, a Level 1 specific theory paper contains:
distractors: 30 is the Level 2 specific paper count.
40 exceeds the PCN specific paper count.
20 is below the PCN specific paper count.
content.explanation: PCN Level 1 specific theory papers have 25 questions; Level 2 specific papers have 30.

content.stem: Under PCN, a Level 2 specific theory paper contains:
distractors: 25 is the Level 1 specific paper count.
40 exceeds the PCN specific paper count.
20 is below the PCN specific paper count.
content.explanation: PCN Level 2 specific theory papers have 30 questions, against 25 at Level 1.

content.stem: Each part of a PCN examination must be passed with a mark of at least:
distractors: The PCN pass mark for each part is 70%.
80% is higher than the PCN requirement.
50% is below the PCN pass mark.
content.explanation: In line with ISO 9712, each part of a PCN examination must be passed at 70%.

content.stem: A PCN certificate is valid for:
distractors: PCN certificates run for five years.
Ten years spans two certification cycles, not one.
Two years is shorter than the PCN validity.
content.explanation: A PCN certificate is valid for five years, in line with ISO 9712.

content.stem: Within the five-year validity, revalidating a PCN certificate without an examination is called:
distractors: Recertification involves examination or structured credit, not a no-exam step.
Reinstatement applies after a certificate has lapsed.
A supplementary adds scope; it is not the no-exam revalidation.
content.explanation: Renewal revalidates a PCN certificate without examination within the five-year period; recertification at expiry is by examination or structured credit.

content.stem: PCN recertification can be achieved by examination or by:
options: Employer attestation on its own letterhead
distractors: An employer letter alone does not recertify a PCN holder.
A fee alone does not satisfy recertification.
Membership of BINDT does not recertify.
content.explanation: PCN recertification is by examination or, for eligible levels, through the structured credit system of documented activity.

content.stem: A PCN recertification application must reach BINDT no sooner than six months and no later than:
options: Any time within the final year before expiry
On the exact day of expiry
distractors: The window closes six weeks before expiry, not a year.
One week is inside the closed window.
Applications are not accepted on the expiry day itself.
content.explanation: PCN recertification applications must arrive no sooner than six months and no later than six weeks before the certificate expires.

content.stem: PCN certification does not by itself authorise the holder to operate; authorisation is given by:
options: BINDT, printed on the certificate itself
distractors: BINDT certifies competence; the employer authorises operation.
The AQB examines; it does not authorise operation.
UKAS accredits the scheme; it does not authorise individuals.
content.explanation: PCN certification attests competence; authorisation to operate is given in writing by the employer, as ISO 9712 requires.
